item.title: Kontrolmatik’s Rise and Fall Burns Turkey’s Retail Traders
item.description: Small-time investor Riza Gundogdu thought he had found the next Tesla Inc. early last year when he invested in shares of Kontrolmatik Enerji ve Muhendislik AS.

item.title: Copper Set for Monthly Gain on Tightening Global Supply Outlook
item.description: Copper headed for a monthly advance on growing signs of tight supply, fueled in part by large flows of material to the US ahead of a highly-anticipated decision by the Trump administration on import tariffs.

item.title: Swiggy, Eternal Stocks Surge as Zepto’s India IPO Hits Roadblock
item.description: Shares of the main competitors to Indian rapid-commerce firm Zepto Ltd. are set for their best month in years after the loss-making company’s planned initial public offering hit a roadblock.

item.title: PBOC’s Weaker Daily Fixing to Temper Yuan Gains, Analysts Say
item.description: China’s central bank set the yuan’s fixing at a weaker-than-expected level, a move that some analysts said may indicate a desire to slow the pace of gains after the currency climbed to a three-year high.

item.title: Asian Stocks Post Biggest Gain in Four Months on AI Optimism
item.description: Asian stocks posted their biggest gain in nearly four months as investors piled into chipmakers, after blockbuster earnings from major tech firms reinforced optimism over AI demand.

item.title: JPY/USD: BOJ Holds Rate Steady And Upgrades View on Economy
item.description: The Bank of Japan kept its policy settings unchanged while signaling less caution about economic growth, pointing to confidence that the economy remains on track for further policy normalization after it lifted its benchmark rate last month to the highest since 1995.

item.title: Bank of Japan Holds Interest Rate Steady at 1% as Expected
item.description: The Bank of Japan kept its policy settings unchanged at the end of its two-day meeting on Friday after lifting its benchmark rate last month to the highest since 1995.

item.title: North Korea’s Economy Expands on Russia Arms Deals, China Trade
item.description: North Korea’s economy expanded for a third straight year in 2025, boosted by arms exports to Russia, stronger trade with China, and Kim Jong Un’s drive to develop regional industries, according to estimates by South Korea’s central bank.

item.title: Philippines to Revamp Bond Pricing Ahead of JPM Index Inclusion
item.description: The Philippines plans to change the way it prices local-currency bonds by removing the impact of withholding tax, a shift that may saddle some existing investors in the nation’s $230 billion market with losses, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Nikkei Weight Cut Shadow Looms Over Advantest After 18% Rally
item.description: Advantest Corp.’s shares may come under selling pressure from passive funds as the Japanese chip-tester maker’s weighting in the Nikkei 225 Stock Average may be lowered at the next review.

item.title: Thailand’s True Internet Data Center Seeks $2 Billion Loan
item.description: Thailand’s True Internet Data Center Co. is seeking an about $2 billion-equivalent loan to build a new facility, according to people familiar with the matter, as the country looks to become a regional hub for artificial intelligence and cloud services.

item.title: Iron Ore Climbs as Traders Weigh Supply Risks From BHP Strike
item.description: Iron ore rose as threat of strike action by BHP Group workers at the export hub of Port Hedland raised concerns about potential supply disruptions, although weak Chinese demand will likely cap price gains.

item.title: Rising US Yields May Complicate RBI’s Strategy on Rates and the Rupee
item.description: If US yields keep rising, the RBI could face growing pressure to keep policy tighter.

item.title: Margin Unwind in Asia Clears Froth, Paving Way for Stock Rebound
item.description: Retail investors have cut their margin debt in South Korea, Taiwan and mainland China, a shift that investors say paves the way for a healthier rebound in Asian stocks.

item.title: JPY/USD: BOJ Leaves Benchmark Rate Unchanged After Yen Intervention
item.description: JPY/USD: BOJ Leaves Benchmark Rate Unchanged After Yen Intervention【原文：JPY/USD: BOJ Leaves Benchmark Rate Unchanged After Yen Intervention】

item.title: Australia’s Social Media Ban Sees Only Small Dip in Teen Users
item.description: Australia’s social media ban for under-16s led to only a marginal reduction in underage users in its first three months, underscoring the lack of enforcement of the world-first law by major platforms.

item.title: China’s Factories, Construction Slump in Sign Slowdown Spreading
item.description: China’s factory activity unexpectedly contracted for the first time in five months and construction slumped to the lowest since the start of the pandemic, pointing to a further loss of momentum in the economy after a slowdown last quarter.

item.title: Milei’s Central Bank Reform Would Ban Financing State Spending
item.description: Argentine President Javier Milei presented a bill in a national TV address Thursday night to reform the central bank so it is prohibited from financing government spending in the future.

item.title: Amazon, Microsoft Results Show AI Spending Spree Remains Solid
item.description: Aggressive AI spending plans by Amazon.com Inc., Microsoft Corp. and Alphabet Inc. provided fresh evidence that demand for chips and related equipment will remain strong, offering relief to a sector that’s been battered in recent days.

item.title: Gold Holds Gain as Japan Currency Intervention Weighs on Dollar
item.description: Gold held a two-day gain, supported by a sharp decline in the US dollar after Japan intervened to bolster the yen.

item.title: SK Hynix Shares Surge in Seoul on US Peer Rally, Chey Purchase
item.description: SK Hynix Inc. shares rebounded Friday, recovering part of this week’s steep losses, as a rally in US semiconductor stocks and a rare share purchase by SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won helped restore investor confidence.

item.title: Stryker Narrows Earnings Outlook as Cyberattack Challenges Goals
item.description: Stryker Corp narrowed the range of its adjusted-earnings outlook for the full year as the medical device manufacturer said it must increase production as well as ship a backlog of equipment to meet its second-half growth targets after a cyberattack in March disrupted operations.

item.title: Tokyo Inflation Quickens, Keeping BOJ on Interest Rate Hike Path
item.description: Tokyo’s inflation pace quickened for a second month, keeping the Bank of Japan on track to raise interest rates again in coming months, with the board widely expected to stand pat on Friday.

item.title: Korea Plans $14 Billion for Wealth Fund’s AI Bets After Rout
item.description: South Korea plans to inject 20 trillion won ($13.9 billion) into its sovereign wealth fund for strategic investments in AI, data centers and infrastructure, expanding its mandate to include domestic assets for the first time following a rout in technology stocks.

item.title: Anthropic AI Models Hacked Three Organizations During Tests
item.description: Anthropic PBC announced that its artificial intelligence models had breached three different organizations during cybersecurity tests that went awry, a little more than a week after its chief rival, OpenAI, disclosed a similar incident.

item.title: Once-Troubled Nio Turns Into Hottest Chinese Carmaker This Year
item.description: China’s largest fully electric SUV is racing up the nation’s sales charts, giving carmaker Nio Inc. a much-needed boost to its finances and bucking the broader downturn that’s gripped the sector.

item.title: Yen Surges After Japan Intervened in Market Again Ahead of BOJ
item.description: The yen soared by the most in more than two years against the dollar after authorities stepped in once again to try and prop up the nation’s sagging currency ahead of the Bank of Japan’s policy decision.

item.title: OpenAI and Anthropic staffers sign call for US to pace AI development
item.description: They’re calling on the US government to help pace their tech’s development.

item.title: Asian Stocks Set to Rise on Tech, Yen Holds Gains: Markets Wrap
item.description: Asian stocks looked set to rise after a rebound in chip shares fueled a Wall Street rally, reviving confidence in the artificial intelligence trade. The yen held onto its gains amid a report Japanese officials intervened to support the currency.

item.title: CoreWeave’s Wild Stock Ride Takes Toll on Its Cost to Finance AI
item.description: CoreWeave Inc. is no stranger to shaking off wild stock-market swings like those of the past few days, when its shares plunged to their lowest level in 14 months only to then stage their sharpest rally of the year.
